children: Basis bids for corn and soybeans shipped by barge to the US Gulf Coast remained generally steady on Tuesday, traders said, as they watched for export demand.
The US Department of Agriculture did not confirm US soybean sales to top importer China in its daily reporting system, after a string of sales over the past two weeks.
China's Sinograin sold 172,240 metric tons of imported soybeans, or 33.7% of the total volume, according to data from consultancy Mysteel.
For corn, the USDA may need to reduce its estimate for US exports following sluggish sales, traders said.
Chicago Board of Trade corn and soybean futures fell as US farmers harvested their crops.
At the Gulf, CIF corn barges loaded in October were bid at 84 cents over CBOT December corn (CZ26) futures, which was steady from Monday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf corn loaded in November were around 98 cents over futures.
CIF soybean barges loaded in October were bid at 108 cents over CBOT November soybean (SX26) futures, which was unchanged from Monday.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybeans loaded in November were about 120 cents over futures.

Traders continued to watch the Brazilian real after the currency on Monday dropped sharply against the US dollar in the wake of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil, the world's biggest soybean supplier. A stronger dollar can make US supplies more expensive for overseas buyers and reduced export competitiveness.
